about: Shared cases for the CFB Model Lab market rules (docs/cfb-lab/METRICS.md §4). supabase/cfb_lab.sql (football/cfb_lab/sql.test.js) and the JavaScript copy (football/cfb_lab/lab_core.js) must reproduce every expected value exactly. Expected values are written by hand; hash_cases digests are sha256 of `rendered` (SCHEMA.md rule 4).

conventions.ids: h(parts) = first 24 hex of sha256(parts rendered and joined with "|"): null -> "", number -> String(Number(x)) (shortest decimal, no trailing zeros, -0 -> 0), boolean -> true/false, timestamp -> UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ, text as is. quote_id = "cfbq_" + h(source, book, game_id ?? provider_event_id, market_type, observed_at) for an ordinary quote, and the same with a sixth part appended for a provider-declared row: h(..., observed_at, "provider_open") when is_provider_open, h(..., observed_at, "provider_close") when is_provider_close (hash_cases pin all three forms); the ingest always computes quote_id and fingerprint and ignores any supplied value; fingerprint = h(home_line, total_points, price_home, price_away, price_over, price_under); line_id = "cfbl_" + h(game_id, kind, book, market_type, rule_version).
conventions.dedupe: Observations are fed one at a time, in the order listed (they are in observed_at order). game_id null is resolved through event_map (newest created_at per source + provider_event_id) BEFORE key and quote_id are computed. key = (source, book, game_id ?? provider_event_id, market_type). REFUSED when the quote cannot be stored (bad source or market_type, no key, spread without home_line, total without total_points, moneyline without a price, is_pregame not the opposite of is_provider_close, both provider flags) or when it is not a provider close and observed_at >= kickoff_ts. Provider-declared rows (is_provider_open or is_provider_close) are WRITTEN only if no row with the same key and the same flag exists, else DUPLICATE. Ordinary rows are compared with the latest ORDINARY row of the key observed before them: WRITTEN when none exists, the fingerprint differs, it is >= 6h older, or kickoff_ts - observed_at <= 3h and it is >= 50 min older (the last two are heartbeats: is_heartbeat = true); else DUPLICATE. `heartbeat` gives is_heartbeat for a written row; `expect_game_id` the stored game_id.
conventions.lines: The quotes of a line case are STORED rows (already past de-duplication): load them as they are (quote_id and fingerprint computed with the rules above) and derive. `expected` is the complete set of lines for the game, compared as a set on every field listed. A per-book row is per (source, book) and its book column is "source:book" (e.g. "odds_api:draftkings"); its n_books is 1. Ordinary pregame quote = is_pregame and not is_provider_open and not is_provider_close and observed_at < kickoff. Per-book OPEN = earliest ordinary quote of the book; per-book CLOSE = latest ordinary quote in [kickoff - 180 min, kickoff) (ties by quote_id ascending). A quote whose raw book is "consensus" (case-insensitive) is a provider average: it gets per-book rows but is left out of CONSENSUS whenever a real book is in the set. Spread is always derived; total and moneyline only when the game has a quote of that market. Values: spread -> home_line, price_home, price_away; total -> total_points, price_home = OVER price, price_away = UNDER price; moneyline -> price_home, price_away. CONSENSUS OPEN observed_at = earliest opener among the books used; CONSENSUS CLOSE observed_at = latest close among the books used. Every non-MISSING CONSENSUS spread row (OPEN and CLOSE, OBSERVED or PROVIDER_DECLARED) carries best_line_home = max(home_line) and best_line_away = -min(home_line) over the books used. PROVIDER_DECLARED (nothing observed): the provider-declared rows of that kind, each book's LATEST, same provider-average rule, observed_at null. MISSING: all values null, n_books 0, observed_at null. Lines are stored at 2 decimals.
conventions.medians: Lines: median; an even count is the mean of the two middle values. Prices: in decimal-odds space, d = 1 + a/100 (a > 0) or 1 + 100/(-a) (a < 0), 0 and null ignored; median of d (even count: (d1 + d2) / 2); back: d >= 2 -> (d - 1) * 100, else -100 / (d - 1); round half away from zero (sign(x) * floor(|x| + 0.5)). IEEE-754 double arithmetic in exactly this order on both sides; no case lands on an exact .5.

dedupe_cases.why: Ordinary change / heartbeat rule far from kickoff. The 6-hour heartbeat is measured from the latest WRITTEN row, not from the latest observation: 16:59 is 5h59m after the 11:00 row and is dropped, 17:00 is exactly 6h and is written as a heartbeat (>= 6h). A line that moves and moves back is written each time, and a price-only change is a change.

dedupe_cases.why: Close-zone heartbeat: once kickoff is 3 hours or less away (kickoff - observed_at <= 3h), an unchanged quote is written when the latest row is 50 minutes or more older. Outside the zone 50 minutes is not enough. A quote observed at or after kickoff is refused.

dedupe_cases.why: Provider-declared closes (is_provider_close = true, is_pregame = false) are the one exception to the kickoff rule: stored after kickoff, at most once per (source, book, game, market). A second declared close for the same key is a duplicate whatever its value; another book is another key. An ordinary quote after kickoff is still refused, and a provider close claiming to be pregame is refused.

observations.why: ordinary pregame quote
the provider's declared close, recorded after kickoff, first for the key
a declared close is stored once per key, even with a different value
another book is another key
an ordinary quote observed after kickoff
a provider close cannot be pregame (is_pregame must be the opposite of is_provider_close)

dedupe_cases.why: Provider-declared openers (is_provider_open = true) are stored at most once per key and are NOT part of the ordinary series: the first ordinary quote after one is still "no earlier row", and later ordinary quotes are compared only with ordinary rows. A provider opener is a pregame row, so it too is refused at or after kickoff.

dedupe_cases.why: Event-map resolution: a quote with game_id null is resolved through cfb_lab_event_map (the NEWEST row per source + provider_event_id wins) BEFORE its key and quote_id are computed, so a resolved quote and the same quote sent with game_id already set share one key. An unmapped provider event keeps game_id null and is keyed by provider_event_id.

dedupe_cases.why: A provider-declared number and an ordinary quote read in the same fetch share (source, book, game, market_type, observed_at). Their quote_ids differ because a provider-declared row's id carries a sixth part ("provider_open" or "provider_close"), so BOTH are written: the declared opener, and the current number as the first ordinary row of the key. An ordinary quote's id has no sixth part and is unchanged.

the current number seen at the same instant: an ordinary row, id without a sixth part, the first ordinary row of the key
the current number unchanged 30 min later
the declared opener again: stored once per key

line_cases.why: Several books with changes and heartbeats, a provider average beside real books, a late opener, a book whose last quote is outside the close window, both window edges, and an even-count total. Close window [16:30:00, 19:30:00). SPREAD OPEN: t0 is the provider average (espn:consensus, 09-28 15:00); the band ends 09-29 15:00 and holds espn:consensus, draftkings, fanduel and caesars (betmgm opened 09-30 09:00, outside it); the provider average is dropped because real books are in the band, so the median is over -3.5, -3.5, -3.0 = -3.5, prices -110/-112/-110 -> -110 and -110/-108/-110 -> -110, best lines max -3.0 / -min 3.5, and observed_at is the FIRST REAL BOOK (draftkings 09-28 18:00), not t0. SPREAD CLOSE: draftkings closes on its 16:30:00 quote (exactly kickoff - 180 min, included) because its 19:30:00 quote is exactly at kickoff (excluded; that row carries kickoff_ts null, which is how it could be stored); fanduel closes on its 19:29 heartbeat (heartbeats count); betmgm at 18:00; caesars last quoted 16:29 (one minute before the window) and has no close; the provider average (18:30) gets its own per-book row but is dropped from CONSENSUS. Median of -4.5, -4.5, -4.0 = -4.5; price_home of -105, -110, +100 in decimal space = -105; price_away of -115, -110, -120 = -115; observed_at = latest used (19:29); best_line_home = max = -4.0, best_line_away = -min = 4.5. TOTAL: prices are the over (price_home) and under (price_away) prices. Both books open 55.5 (-110/-110); close 56.5 and 57.0 -> even count, mean = 56.75; over -110 and -108 -> -108.99 -> -109, under -110 and -112 -> -110.99 -> -111.

Even counts and prices that straddle +/-100, in decimal-odds space. SPREAD OPEN: lines +1.0 and +1.5 -> +1.25; price_home -110 and -105 -> decimals 1.909091 and 1.952381, mean 1.930736 -> -107.44 -> -107; price_away -110 and -115 -> mean 1.889328 -> -112.44 -> -112; best lines +1.5 / -1.0. SPREAD CLOSE: +1.0 and +1.5 -> +1.25; price_home +105 and -105 -> decimals 2.05 and 1.952381, mean 2.001190 -> +100.12 -> +100 (the mean of the American numbers would be 0, which is not a price); price_away -125 and -115 -> -119.79 -> -120; best_line_home = +1.5, best_line_away = -min(+1.0, +1.5) = -1.0 (the away side lays 1 at the best book). MONEYLINE: the value is the price pair. The OPEN band is draftkings and fanduel (caesars first quoted 10-11 22:30, beyond t0 + 24h, so it has a per-book OPEN but is outside the band): +105 and +115 -> decimals 2.05 and 2.15, mean 2.10 -> +110; -125 and -135 -> -129.81 -> -130. CLOSE: three books, +110/+105/+115 -> +110 and -130/-125/-135 -> -130, observed_at = caesars 22:30 (latest used). Moneyline lines carry no home_line and no best lines.

Provider-declared close fallback. The only book with ordinary quotes last quoted at 10-17 20:00, before the close window [13:00, 16:00), so no book has a close and there is no per-book CLOSE row. The consensus close falls back to the provider-declared closes (each book's latest): espn:espnbet declared -8.0 and a provider average (cfbd:consensus) declared -8.5; the provider average is dropped because a real book declared one, so the CONSENSUS CLOSE is -8.0, quality PROVIDER_DECLARED, n_books 1, observed_at NULL (a declared number has no observation time of its own), best lines -8.0 / 8.0. The opener is observed normally.

Provider-declared opener only, and nothing at all for the close. With no ordinary pregame quote there is no per-book OPEN (a provider-declared opener is not an observed opener); the CONSENSUS OPEN falls back to the declared openers: espn:espnbet -2.5 and a provider average espn:consensus -3.0, the provider average dropped -> -2.5, PROVIDER_DECLARED, n_books 1, observed_at NULL, best lines -2.5 / 2.5. There is no close of any kind, so the CONSENSUS CLOSE is MISSING: every value null, n_books 0.

No market data at all. The spread is always derived, so a game with no quote gets a MISSING CONSENSUS OPEN and a MISSING CONSENSUS CLOSE (values null, n_books 0, observed_at null) and nothing else; total and moneyline are derived only for markets the game has a quote in. (Postgres learns of a game with no quotes from its LIVE prediction, so the SQL test registers one; register_with_prediction says so.)

Only provider averages, from two providers. With no real sportsbook the provider averages are used rather than dropped. A per-book row is per (source, book): cfbd:consensus and espn:consensus are two books. OPEN: t0 = cfbd:consensus 11-03 12:00 (-10.0); espn:consensus first appears 11-08 16:00, outside t0 + 24h, so the CONSENSUS OPEN is -10.0 from one book. CLOSE (window [14:00, 17:00)): cfbd:consensus -10.5 at 15:00 and espn:consensus -11.0 at 16:00 -> median -10.75, n_books 2, observed_at 16:00, best_line_home = max = -10.5, best_line_away = -min = 11.0.

price_median_cases.why: straddles +/-100: decimals 1.952381 and 2.05, mean 2.001190 -> +100.12 -> +100 (the American numbers would average to 0)
two plus prices: mean of decimals 2.10 -> +110
0 and null are ignored: -110 and -120 -> decimals 1.909091 and 1.833333, mean 1.871212 -> -114.78 -> -115
